reason: The pancreatic islet's sensing cells are positioned to respond to the glucose-rich blood after a meal.
expectation: The cells will detect the higher glucose and initiate a hormonal response.

effect: The after-meal condition triggers insulin release, which reaches both muscle and liver; I can follow one of those targets next.
reaction: The separate target branches make the next choice clear.
reason: The liver is an insulin target and contains glycogen, suggesting a route for storing meal glucose.
expectation: Insulin will promote glucose storage as liver glycogen.

alternatives.reason: Muscle is also shown receiving insulin and may take up glucose.

effect: The liver stores glucose as glycogen under insulin signalling, without the muscle-style transporter insertion shown in the description.
reaction: The distinction between liver and muscle glucose entry is useful.
reason: Muscle is the other target shown receiving insulin, so it is the natural next part of the after-meal response.
expectation: Insulin will promote glucose uptake by muscle, likely involving transporter insertion.

effect: Insulin increases muscle glucose transport, and its release signal weakens as blood glucose falls; the after-meal goal is complete.
reaction: The feedback connection clarifies how the response eases.
reason: The same pancreatic sensing cells can respond to the lower glucose level between meals.
expectation: The islet will release a hormone that helps keep blood glucose available.

effect: Lower glucose prompted glucagon release from alpha cells, with the liver highlighted as its target.
reaction: The contrast with the after-meal insulin response is clear.
reason: The liver contains glycogen and is the target of the between-meal glucagon signal.
expectation: Glucagon will promote glycogen breakdown and glucose release into the blood.

effect: Glucagon promoted liver glycogen breakdown and glucose release, with its stimulation diminishing as blood glucose rose; both goals are complete.
reaction: The feedback makes the between-meal response clear.

mostWorthwhile.text: Comparing insulin’s effects on liver storage and muscle uptake was most worthwhile: the planned pictures distinguish liver glucose entry from the increased muscle membrane transporters.

leastWorthwhile.text: The initial insulin-release step was relatively straightforward; its main value was setting up the more informative target responses.

surprise.text: The liver picture explicitly distinguished its glucose entry from muscle-style transporter insertion, a useful clarification.

arbitrary.text: No action felt arbitrary: the islet and target-organ connections were visible. Glycogen’s role was illustrated, though the term itself was not defined in words in this chapter.

continue.text: Yes. I would continue to see more comparisons that connect organ responses to feedback, as this chapter did for glucose regulation.
